title: quiet-queue-smokecheck-notes-2024-04-09
content:
Meeting: Quiet Queue smoke-check + quick benchmark sync
Date: 2024-04-09 (notes updated 2024-04-12)
Owner: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Connor, Marta, Benji, (quick drop-in from SRE: Priya)
Context / why: We observed unexplained p95 spikes in the quiet-queue shadow runs last week when traffic dropped below 15qps on A100 pools. This doc captures the quick smoke tests we ran, initial hypotheses, raw numbers, and immediate next steps.

Agenda:
- Reproduce p95 spike with isolated quiet-queue workload
- Check KV cache temperature and cold-path hit-rate during quiet periods
- Validate batching heuristics when queueing is sparse
- Capture telemetry pointers for follow-up triage

Quick summary of result:
- Reproduced a narrow p95 bump (~2.6x baseline) during a 3–8 qps window on the A100-old pool.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~93% to ~68% on those runs (likely due to prefix churn from mixed sessions).
- Small-batch path (batch size <=2) latency median unchanged, tail degraded. Evidence points at intermittent serialization stalls in the sequencer + microbatch flattening logic.

What we ran (concise):
- Harness: local bench runner -> shadow traffic generator (repo/benchmarks/e2e/quiet-queue)
- Model: rdx-7b-quant (fp16 baseline); sequence len distribution: mean 64, tail 512 (samples seeded)
- Hardware: A100-v4 (old), 4 GPUs, 16 instances seeded to shadow pool
- Workload pattern: steady 3qps for 10m -> burst to 60qps for 2m -> back to 5qps for 15m
- Instrumentation: per-request trace, batch composition logs, KV cache metrics, sequencer queue depth, python-level GC counts, grpc threadpool wait stats

Selected raw numbers (median over 3 repeats):
- Baseline 60qps period: p50=18ms, p90=57ms, p95=82ms, throughput stable at 58 qps
- Quiet 3–5qps period: p50=20ms, p90=120ms, p95=210ms (spike episodes), throughput nominal but many small microbatches
- KV cache hit-rate: 93% (burst) -> 68% (quiet)
- Average batch size: 3.6 (burst) -> 1.8 (quiet)

Observations / quick hypotheses:
1) Sequencer stall coupled with microbatch flattening: when a few inflight requests exist, the sequencer sometimes holds a batch slot waiting for N but ends up flushing small batches; internal timer misfire causes a ~120–300ms stall on a subset of requests.
2) KV cache churn: the quiet period had more mixed-session patterns in trace; prefix keys evicted or not reused causing more kernel cold-paths. That increases per-token CPU work and memory ops, amplifying tail.
3) GC / python scheduling jitter: small but visible correlation between python GC runs and tail spikes in the traces (further instrumentation required).

Immediate mitigations tried during the smokecheck (live experiments):
- Disabled microbatch flattening heuristic (flag: --disable-flatten) -> p95 improved by ~30% in quiet window, but p50 unchanged. Good quick toggle for emergency.
- Increased sequencer flush timer from 5ms -> 1ms -> actually lowering the threshold improved tail for single-request batches but increased total GPU kernel launches (cost impact).
- Slightly raised KV cache retention TTL for prefixes (config toggle) -> restored hit-rate to ~85% and reduced p95 by ~18%.

Telemetry & artifacts captured (where to look):
- traces/quiet-queue/2024-04-09/run-01 (s3 path in runbook)
- bench logs: repo/benchmarks/quiet-queue/2024-04-09/*.log
- dashboard panels updated: Serving Runtime > Quiet Queue p95, KV cache hit heatmap, Sequencer flush timings

Decisions and tradeoffs discussed:
- Rollout of disable-flatten as a hotfix for affected customers: acceptable as 1-week mitigant but increases GPU kernel overhead and cost per token. Prefer to gate with canary and rollback if cost delta > 8%.
- Prefer longer-term fix: make sequencer timers adaptive (based on current queue depth + recent flush variance) and improve prefix retention heuristics.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Aisha: Prepare emergency toggle PR for disable-flatten + smoke-run automation (ETA: 24 hours)
- Connor: Add microsecond-resolution sequencer metrics + event id tagging so we can correlate stall causes (ETA: 3 working days)
- Marta: Run extended A/B cost test for disable-flatten across two pools (A100-old and A100-new) and capture cost delta (ETA: 5 working days)
- Benji: Add targeted KV cache heatmap to console (panel + alert when hit-rate < 80%) (ETA: 4 days)
- Priya (SRE): Prepare canary steps and rollback checklist for toggling in prod shadow pool (ETA: 48 hours)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did quiet-window have more mixed-session prefixes? Is it traffic-pattern dependent (client-side keepalive) or an artifact of shadow replay randomness? Need to inspect client session ids in traces.
- Does the disable-flatten toggle interact badly with batching heuristics for large-seq workloads? Need negative tests.
- Should we consider increasing default KV prefix TTL globally or make it per-tenant? Cost and memory implications to be evaluated.

Notes to self / informal:
- Ran into flaky bench harness where one runner lost rps clocking -> file the harness bug after this triage (ticket: SRV-4899).
- Logging verbosity increase for sequencer helped root cause but produced a lot of noise; revert after capture.

Next sync: quick follow-up standup in 48 hours to decide on hotfix rollout; include product SLA owner in decision if canary passes.

Attachments referenced in this doc: trace snapshots, bench logs, short flame graphs (stored in runbook links).

Status: draft — will update after hotfix PR and canary results.
